MAYUR SANJAY SAWANT · ROBOTICS & CONTROL RESEARCHER Making autonomous motion reliable.

I develop feedback control methods that help robots navigate around obstacles and move safely through constrained environments.

Explore my research ↗View CV ↗ Postdoctoral ResearcherLakehead University · Thunder Bay, Canada WATCH THE RESEARCH IN MOTION ▶ROBOT EXPERIMENT · TURTLEBOT 4Autonomous navigation ↗ ▶FLIGHT EXPERIMENT · QDRONE 2Dynamic obstacle avoidance ↗ All experiments & simulations ↗ RESEARCH AREASRobotics, control, and geometry.

I am a postdoctoral researcher in Electrical and Computer Engineering at Lakehead University. I earned my PhD from Western University in 2024, where I worked on hybrid feedback control for autonomous robot navigation.

Explore all research ↗ 01Obstacle avoidance

Feedback controllers for navigation around convex and nonconvex obstacles, from planar spaces to higher dimensions.

Explore this work ↗ 02Dynamic navigation

Extending kinematic motion planners to systems with velocity and acceleration.

Explore this work ↗ 03Constrained stabilization

Stabilization on spheres while respecting geometric constraints.

I welcome conversations about feedback control and robotic navigation.

docs.title: Research
docs.text: I study how to make autonomous motion safe and reliable in environments with obstacles and geometric constraints. My work spans hybrid feedback control, dynamic navigation, and stabilization on manifolds.

docs.title: Obstacle avoidance
docs.text:
I design hybrid feedback controllers that guide robots toward a goal while avoiding obstacles. My research covers planar and three-dimensional environments, convex and nonconvex obstacles, and higher-dimensional spaces.

Selected papers: Planar convex obstacles (2023) · Nonconvex obstacles (2024) · Three-dimensional navigation (2025) · N-dimensional convex obstacles (2026) · Watch experiments & simulations

docs.title: Dynamic navigation
docs.text:
Kinematic motion planners specify where a robot should move. My current work examines how to carry those planning ideas into systems with second-order dynamics, where velocity and acceleration affect the motion.

Selected papers: From Kinematic Motion Planners to Dynamic Autonomous Navigation with Obstacle Avoidance · Adapting First-order Motion Planners to Second-order Dynamical Systems · Watch the QDrone experiment

docs.title: Constrained stabilization
docs.text:
I develop stabilization methods for motion on spheres under geometric constraints. The problems include conic, star-shaped, and geodesically convex regions.

Selected papers: Constrained Stabilization on the n-Sphere with Conic and Star-shaped Constraints · Dynamic Stabilization on the n-sphere with Star-shaped Constraints
